body.statement:
Lemma (sound supplied rational-witness precheck).  For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), all membership and signature tests at the supplied table \(p^{\circ}\) in the nonzero-normal-form branch of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) terminate by exact rational arithmetic.  Whenever that precheck returns \((D_0,D,p^{\circ})\), one has \(p^{\circ}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^\Omega\) and, for at least one outcome cell \(y\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ});
\]
hence the two represented-DAG intervention vectors differ.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\).  That definition requires an exact-rational verification of
\[
 p^{\circ}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}. \tag{1}
\]
In particular, \(\mathfrak D\) is a nonempty finite family, and \(D_0\) and every \(D\in\mathfrak D\) are represented DAGs.  Because \(V\) and all state spaces \(\Omega_v\) are finite, the cell set \(\Omega\), the collections \(\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)\) and \(\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)\), the DAG family \(\mathfrak D\), and the set of outcome cells \(\prod_{v\in Y}\Omega_v\) are all finite.

We first prove termination and exactness of the precheck.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\), membership of \(p^{\circ}\) in \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) consists of the finite collection of tests
\[
 \sum_{z\in\Omega}p^{\circ}_z=1,\qquad
 p^{\circ}_z>0\quad(z\in\Omega),\qquad
 g(p^{\circ})=0\quad(g\in\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)), \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{g\in\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)}g(p^{\circ})^2>0
 \quad\text{for every \(c\) such that \(\mathcal I(c)=0\)}. \tag{3}
\]
Every expression in (2)--(3) is rational: \(p^{\circ}\) has rational coordinates by (1), and the determinantal generators have rational coefficients by their construction.  Likewise, \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\) give integer polynomials \(A_{D,y}\), \(B_{D,y}\), and
\[
 F_{D,y}=A_{D,y}B_{D_0,y}-A_{D_0,y}B_{D,y}. \tag{4}
\]
Consequently, evaluation of every recorded denominator and every \(F_{D,y}\) at \(p^{\circ}\) produces a rational number.  A rational equality or strict inequality is decided after finitely many integer additions, multiplications, greatest-common-divisor reductions, and sign comparisons: explicitly, after writing a tested rational as \(a/b\) with \(a\in\mathbb Z\), \(b\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), equality to zero is equivalent to \(a=0\), and positivity is equivalent to \(a>0\).  There are only finitely many tests by the preceding finiteness observations.  Hence every membership, denominator, and signature test performed at \(p^{\circ}\) by the supplied-witness precheck in \(\mathrm{def{:}sparse\text{-}simid}\) terminates and is exact.

Suppose now that this precheck returns \((D_0,D,p^{\circ})\).  Its return condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}sparse\text{-}simid}\), together with the certified membership (1), gives an outcome cell \(y\) such that
\[
 F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\ne 0. \tag{5}
\]
Strict positivity in (1) implies that every observed marginal is strictly positive: for every nonempty marginalization index set and every fixed assignment, the relevant marginal is a finite sum of strictly positive cell probabilities.  The denominators in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) are products of precisely such uncancelled observed marginal factors.  Therefore
\[
 B_{D,y}(p^{\circ})>0,
 \qquad B_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})>0. \tag{6}
\]
Using \(T_{D,y}=A_{D,y}/B_{D,y}\), (4), and (6), direct subtraction yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 T_{D,y}(p^{\circ})-T_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})
 &=\frac{A_{D,y}(p^{\circ})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})
          -A_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})B_{D,y}(p^{\circ})}
         {B_{D,y}(p^{\circ})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})}\\
 &=\frac{F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})}
         {B_{D,y}(p^{\circ})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})}
 \ne 0, \tag{7}
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last inequality follows from (5)--(6).  Thus the two intervention vectors differ in their \(y\)-coordinate.

Finally, (1) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}law\text{-}redundancy}\) imply that the same observed law \(p^{\circ}\) is Markov to both \(D_0\) and \(D\).  Under the DAG intervention semantics encoded by the truncated factorization in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), the two quantities in (7) are respectively the \(y\)-cell probabilities of the intervention law under those two represented DAGs.  Hence the returned triple is a valid common-observed-law ambiguity certificate, and the represented-DAG intervention vectors are unequal, as claimed.
